This is quite simply not true. First, most connections are HTTPS nowdays. For those that are not, machine identifiers are not going to be transmitted with the majority of requests. If Firefox is checking for updates, you can see exactly what's in the request through packet monitoring, and it includes OS and version, but not much else. Finally, there will be many of these requests coming off of a node. Correlating these is not a trivial task, and not one suited to doing en masse.

With security, you need to define a hypothetical adversary. If your adversary is a government specifically trying to find out what you're looking at, they'll do it by correlating the packets coming into the VPN node with the ones coming out, and they can do this by controlling your ISP and the egress of the VPN. If your adversary is Google/Facebook doing mass data collection, then a VPN secures your IP from them, which is a major part of your digital fingerprint.
Plus every extra security measure you take isn't meant to make you completely secure; that's impossible. The whole point is to make it slightly harder or costly for the other person to do so.
